subject: FinSecure operational controls — support access rehearsal & retention thresholds
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finsecure.com>, Brian Cole <brian.cole@finsecure.com>, Sasha Boyd <sasha@fivestack.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FinSecure operational controls — support access rehearsal & retention thresholds

Hi Maya / Brian / Sasha,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation. I wanted to capture the items we agreed to surface and get clarifications so we can map them to the contract/security annex: 

Quick recap (from our side):
- Scope: Redwood will host inference for FinSecure production traffic; some conversation logs will include PII (names, account ids).
- Ask: confirm acceptable retention thresholds for conversation logs and any hard exclusions (PII never stored) or redaction expectations.
- Support access: you asked about break-glass for incident investigations — we typically offer SSO + short-lived elevated roles and audit logging. Need to confirm FinSecure's approval model (one-click, two-person auth).
- Residency & logging: confirm region(s) of processing/storage you require and SIEM/Log push expectations for audit trail.

To move fast we need three clarifications from you:
1) Retention windows: acceptable default for logs that may contain PII (options we can support: 7 days / 30 days / 90 days / custom TTL + redact-on-ingest). Please indicate preferred option and any regulatory hold exceptions.
2) Support access model: is break-glass allowed with a single emergency approver, or do you require two-person approval? Do you require an out-of-band justification ticket?
3) Residency & evidence: required processing region(s) (US/EU/APAC) and the evidentiary artifacts you need for compliance review (SOC2 report, access logs, SIEM ingestion proof).

Attachments: FinSecure_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (we filled Sections 1–3 but left the retention/SCIM bits blank) and breakglass_scenarios.xlsx (draft scenarios to align).

Proposed next steps:
- You reply with the three clarifications above by EOD Tue 4/6 if possible.
- We schedule a 30-min runbook walkthrough with your ops/security team (propose Wed 4/7 or Thu 4/8).

Thanks — I flagged Vivek and Monica who will own the follow-ups on our side.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwoodinference.com

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finsecure.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Sasha Boyd <sasha@fivestack.io>
Cc: Brian Cole <brian.cole@finsecure.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinSecure operational controls — support access rehearsal & retention thresholds

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming answers below so you can update the annex and the questionnaire: 

1) Retention windows
- Default conversational logs that contain PII: 90 days.
- We are open to a 30-day retention in a scoped pilot but enterprise requirement is 90 days.
- For regulatory holds (investigations/subpoenas) we will issue a preservation hold; please confirm you can suspend deletion on request and provide exported evidence.

2) Support access (break-glass)
- Break-glass is allowed for severity P1 incidents only.
- Approval model: JIT ephemeral elevation with a two-person approval (one oncall + one security approver). We require an automatic ticket (Jira or internal ID) and a mandatory justification recorded in the audit event.
- All break-glass events must emit full request/response logs to our SIEM (Splunk) and include operator identity + justification.

3) Residency & evidence
- Processing: Primary in US (IAD) with the option to restrict EU workloads to eu-west-1 if requested.
- Required artifacts: latest SOC2 Type II report, access logs (at least 365 days retention for audit logs), and a sample of redaction/PII-handling summary for verification.

I attached a completed page for Section 2 of your questionnaire with our default retention/approval model. We'll pull together the SOC2 request route via procurement — Brian is looping in procurement but he is out this afternoon.

Happy to join the walkthrough next week. Wed 4/7 works for my team.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of InfoSec | FinSecure
maya.singh@finsecure.com
Attachment: FinSecure_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (page 4 filled)

Proposed workshop on Wed 4/7 10:30–11:00 PST: runbook review + break-glass tabletop (we'll bring scripted scenarios from breakglass_scenarios.xlsx). Please confirm; if Wed doesn't work we can move to Thu 4/8 same time.

Thanks — Monica and I will coordinate the demo pieces and deliver the runbook draft.
